title: DPF discovery and generation workflows
introduction:
Use these procedures with the experimental `l8k discover --target dpf` CLI. The DPU estate is separate from Host Network Operator deployment. Start with **inventory mode**. Optional management mode adds temporary Linux/amd64 network probes as described below. Discovery collects facts and writes a handoff. It does not create VMs, install Kubernetes or DPF, configure DPUServices, change firmware, enroll trust, or start a DPF deployment.

For complete field and error details, see [DPF discovery reference](dpf-discovery.md). Each diagram follows the same steps as its procedure. Commands are examples to run deliberately from a machine with direct access to your selected endpoints. Discovery itself does not deploy. HBN-BGP also has separate [generation](#hbn-bgp-generation) and [deployment](#hbn-bgp-deployment) procedures.

workflows.title: Collect the first inventory
workflows.introduction: Use this workflow when you know the host access addresses. Explicit DPU BMC endpoints and verified administrator privileges are required for a complete inventory. Without explicit DPU endpoints, Launch Kit derives BlueField card records from host inventory and leaves their access bindings unknown; host-only or ARM-only discovery retains partial evidence and exits nonzero.

steps.title: CLI machine: choose sources and access inputs
steps.body:
Choose each source explicitly: a host operating system over SSH or its BMC over Redfish; choose the DPU BMC over Redfish for a complete run. DPU ARM SSH is available for partial evidence but cannot verify BMC administrator privileges. A selected source must succeed; Launch Kit does not silently replace failed Redfish access with SSH. Host SSH can supply host-to-card identity in Zero Trust when PCI/VPD access is available. ARM SSH needs a booted, reachable DPU operating system. Neither access path proves trusted DPU state.

| Input | What you supply or allow Launch Kit to determine |
| --- | --- |
| Always required | At least one host endpoint and explicit DPU BMC endpoints with administrator credentials for completion; the source type; a credential alias, username, and password reference or SSH key reference for each selected endpoint. Addresses and credentials are not guessed. |
| Required for SSH | A verified `knownHostsFile`; direct connectivity from the CLI machine. SSH port defaults to `22`; ambient SSH config, agents and ProxyJump are not used. |
| Conditional | DPU ARM SSH for partial OS measurements; a private CA for Redfish when system trust is insufficient; `systemURI` if a BMC exposes several Systems. |
| Optional | A management kubeconfig for additional observations. Inventory needs none, but an explicitly supplied kubeconfig must work. |
| Defaultable | `dpf.release` defaults to `26.4.0`; Redfish certificate verification is enabled; SSH `sudo` defaults to `false`. Choose `discovery.probes.mode: inventory` for this workflow to omit temporary management-network probes. HBN-BGP already defaults to inventory mode. |
| Discovered | Host/system and card identities, host-to-DPU associations, visible hardware/software/network observations, and optional local BMC address hints. |

Use an account whose own session proves its effective administrator role. If session Roles is absent, local authentication must be established by an explicit trusted local session `UserAuthenticationSource`. A current `LocalAccountAuth: Enabled` policy alone cannot prove how an existing session authenticated. Disabled local authentication and explicitly external session sources are unsupported; Fallback/LocalFirst require the explicit local session source. Missing origin plus missing Roles cannot inherit privileges from a same-named local administrator. Discovery reports unverifiable proof as partial without replacing a complete handoff.

Do not provide product versions as measured facts. The selected release supplies the software bill of materials (BOM); discovery measures installed versions separately. Omitted or null `dpf.release` uses the pinned default; an empty or unknown release is rejected.

All network connections start from the machine where you run `l8k`. Host and DPU endpoints do not need to connect to each other for this workflow.

| Connection from the CLI machine | Where the operation runs | What it provides |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SSH to the selected host | Host operating system | Host identity, installed card serials and available host/card facts |
| SSH to the selected DPU ARM address | DPU operating system | DPU identity, local hardware/network facts, and optionally its BMC address through local IPMI |
| HTTPS to a selected host or DPU BMC | That BMC's Redfish service | System/card identity, host PCI/reset information and available named DPU firmware versions |
| HTTPS to the management API, only if a kubeconfig is supplied | Existing management Kubernetes API | Cluster identity, version and nodes, plus optional storage and advertised DPF API information |
| No remote connection | CLI machine | Read input/trust/lease files, match identities, compare software requirements and save results |

Choose SSH or Redfish separately for each endpoint. Selecting host Redfish does not run tools in the host OS. Selecting DPU SSH does not log in to DPU Redfish. The [collection step](#initial-inventory-collect) lists the operations for each choice.

steps.title: CLI and endpoint administrators: prepare access
steps.body:
Put passwords in an environment variable or a private file, and SSH private keys and known-hosts entries in files under your control. Reference them from YAML; do not put password values in command-line arguments. File references are relative to that YAML file. Verify SSH keys and Redfish CA trust through your normal provisioning process.

For SSH inventory, ask the endpoint administrator to make the required read tools and permissions available before the run. Host identity/PCI collection uses tools such as `dmidecode` and `lspci`; DPU identity additionally uses `ipmitool`. Optional hardware checks use `mlxfwmanager`, `mlxconfig`, `mlxprivhost` and `systemctl`; network checks use existing `ip`, resolver and LLDP tools where available. Tool availability and access differ between host and ARM operating systems.

Set `ssh.sudo: true` only where noninteractive elevated reads are authorized and configured. Launch Kit then uses `sudo -n`; it never prompts for a sudo password, installs tools, changes privileges or repairs device settings. Missing tools, denied permissions and unsupported or malformed outputs keep specific reason codes and explanations. Required identity failures stop a complete inventory; optional unknown observations remain visible for review.

Prepare a DPU BMC account that is enabled, unlocked and does not require a password change, with all five standard Administrator privileges. A custom role with those privileges is accepted; names alone are insufficient. Discovery verifies the session, unique matching account and linked role using read requests. Handle password changes separately before rerunning; discovery never rotates passwords or tests privileges through writes.

Passwords may use an environment reference supplied for the invocation or a `passwordRef.file` pointing to an owner-only UTF-8 password file. Environment variables are convenient for automation but can be inherited or exposed by diagnostics. File references avoid that export but remain plaintext files: keep them private and outside version control. Discovery saves references, never secret values.

steps.title: CLI machine: create the inventory configuration
steps.body:
Save this example as `dpf-site.yaml`, replacing the documentation address and credential paths with your host values. It uses host SSH and DPU BMC Redfish and requires no Kubernetes cluster. Ensure the listed files exist before running.

```yaml
dpf:
  release: 26.4.0
credentials:
  host-reader:
    username: inventory
    privateKeyRef: {file: ./credentials/host-key}
  dpu-maintainer:
    username: bmc-maintainer
    passwordRef: {env: DPU_BMC_PASSWORD}
discovery:
  hosts:
    - credentialRef: host-reader
      ssh:
        address: 192.0.2.21:22
        knownHostsFile: ./credentials/known_hosts
        sudo: true
  dpus:
    - bmcEndpoint: https://192.0.2.11
      credentialRef: dpu-maintainer
  probes:
    mode: inventory
```

For DPU ARM observations, use the SSH shape instead; ARM-only DPU input produces partial inventory with a nonzero exit because it cannot prove BMC administrator privileges. For Redfish, use `bmcEndpoint` and a password credential reference instead of `ssh`; see the [complete access examples](dpf-discovery.md#inputs-and-invocation). Each endpoint has exactly one access source. Plain YAML is the CLI input, not a Kubernetes object. Do not copy previously observed `inventory` facts into a new seed as user assertions.

steps.title: CLI machine: start discovery
steps.body:
Choose a new output path for the first run. Run from a machine that can reach every selected endpoint and read the referenced files.

```bash
l8k discover --target dpf --user-config dpf-site.yaml \
  --save-cluster-config dpf-discovered.yaml --output json \
  > discovery.json 2> discovery.log
```

Record the process exit status as well as the files. `discovery.json` contains the final result; progress and diagnostics go to `discovery.log`. The command creates its own run directory next to the requested YAML. It does not send credentials to addresses found during collection. Redfish uses a temporary login session and deletes that session; SSH runs read commands on explicitly selected endpoints.

While this command runs, Launch Kit performs the collection and matching steps below automatically. You do not need to run the listed remote commands yourself. The example contacts the host over SSH and the explicitly selected DPU BMC over Redfish. Host-only input contacts no DPU endpoint and returns partial evidence with a nonzero exit.

Watch live source/check status on stderr: RUNNING is emitted before the operation, followed by its result. Endpoint names/addresses distinguish concurrent work. To keep progress visible with JSON, redirect stdout only (`>discover.json`). Add `--log-level debug` for stage timing or `--log-level trace` for request/tool metadata; `2>discover.log` saves these messages instead of displaying them. Quiet suppresses progress.

steps.title: Selected host, DPU and BMC: read identity and facts
steps.body:
Launch Kit uses the configured connection for each endpoint. Required identity reads and DPU BMC administrator verification must succeed to complete inventory. Optional reads add facts; a missing tool, denied operation or unsupported response leaves an explained gap instead of silently passing the check. After collecting optional facts, Launch Kit rereads identity to detect a changed or replaced device. If an optional SSH command times out, Launch Kit retains the reason and reconnects to the same configured endpoint with the same credentials and verified host keys before the next read. It does not retry the timed-out command. Failed reconnection, a failed identity reread or an expired overall deadline still prevents complete inventory.

**On a host selected through SSH**

| Read performed on the host | Purpose and result | Required or optional |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dmidecode -s system-uuid` | Identifies the physical host. | Required |
| `lspci -Dnn -d 15b3:` and per-card `lspci -D -vv -s <PCI-address>` | Finds NVIDIA network cards, their PCI locations and available card serial/slot information. | PCI enumeration is required; a selected DPU needs a usable serial for host-to-card matching. Missing serials remain visible. |
| Linux PCI device files | Reads each function's network interface, driver and NUMA location. | Optional |
| `systemctl show rshim --property=LoadState --property=ActiveState` | Reports whether the host's RShim service is present and active. It does not start the service or use it to access a DPU. | Optional |

**On a DPU ARM operating system selected through SSH**

| Read performed on the DPU ARM OS | Purpose and result | Required or optional |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dmidecode -s system-serial-number` and `ipmitool fru print 0` | Reads system and built-in card records; their serials must agree. Also records available model/board information. | Required for DPU identity |
| `ipmitool lan print` | Reads the local BMC's configured LAN address over local IPMI. | Optional |
| `lspci -Dnn -d 15b3:` and per-card `lspci -D -vv -s <PCI-address>` | Locates ARM-visible NVIDIA cards and available card serials before associating hardware readings with them. | Optional |
| `mlxprivhost -d <PCI-address> q --full` | Reports host privilege restrictions, such as restricted access or disabled RShim, for a visible BlueField. | Optional |

Local IPMI is an operation **from the DPU ARM OS to its local BMC**, not an HTTPS login from the CLI. The returned BMC address is recorded, but Launch Kit does not connect to it or send it credentials. Host and ARM PCI addresses are local to different operating systems and need not match.

**On each selected host or DPU ARM OS, through SSH**

| Read performed on that OS | Purpose and result |
| --- | --- |
| `mlxfwmanager --version` | Records the installed MFT tool version. |
| `mlxfwmanager --query -d <PCI-address>` | Queries the specific visible card's current NIC firmware and PSID. |
| `mlxconfig -d <PCI-address> q <parameter>` | Reads `INTERNAL_CPU_OFFLOAD_ENGINE`, `INTERNAL_CPU_RSHIM` and `NUM_OF_VFS` on visible BlueFields. These results are next-boot settings, not proof of the running mode. |
| `hostname`, `cat /etc/os-release`, `ip -j address show`, `ip -j -4 route show` | Reports the OS, local addresses and IPv4 routes. |
| `ip -j link show`, `ip -j -d link show`, `ip -j neighbor show` | Reports MACs, bridge/member relationships, available link details and neighbors already known to that OS. It does not scan the subnet. |
| `cat /etc/resolv.conf`, `readlink -f /etc/resolv.conf`, `resolvectl dns`, `resolvectl domain` | Reports configured DNS servers, search domains, per-link DNS and the resolver configuration in use. |
| Selected `server=` and `no-resolv` settings in `/etc/dnsmasq.conf` and `/etc/dnsmasq.d/*.conf` | Reports local dnsmasq DNS forwarding configuration. This is separate from reading a DHCP lease snapshot on the CLI machine. |
| `lldpctl -f keyvalue` | Reports neighbors already available from the local LLDP service. |

These hardware and network reads are optional. `<PCI-address>` comes from that same OS's card inventory; Launch Kit queries each card separately. In Zero Trust, the host may be unable to query a restricted card even when `mlxfwmanager` is installed. That limitation is reported; it does not cause an automatic connection to the DPU. Tools must be installed on the OS where the command runs, not merely on the CLI machine. When configured, protected hardware reads use `sudo -n`; tools are never installed or settings changed by discovery.

**On a selected host or DPU BMC, through HTTPS Redfish**

The CLI creates a temporary session and reads system and card inventory. Host BMC reads locate cards associated with the selected host and retain advertised reset types; they do not collect host firmware/time/NTP or DPU-only component placeholders. DPU BMC reads identify that DPU, query available firmware components and verify the authenticated session account and linked role through AccountService. All five standard Administrator privileges and enabled/unlocked/no-password-change state are required; denied or unverifiable evidence fails closed. The supported BF4/B4240 reader also records an optional PSID from the selected System or identity-selected chassis AssetTag, with authenticated reads and a final reread. Missing PSID stays unknown; invalid, contradictory or changed fields remain unavailable for consumers requiring PSID. No PSID is guessed from the model. No SSH commands run in either OS for this choice. System/card identity is required; optional component versions may remain unknown. A firmware version is not assumed to be running unless the BMC explicitly identifies it as active. The CLI deletes its session afterward and reports any cleanup failure. It does not change passwords, roles, firmware, NTP, power or trust settings.

**At the management Kubernetes API, if configured**

The CLI reads the cluster identity from `kube-system`, the Kubernetes version and the node list, including control-plane membership and reported readiness. These reads are required when you supply a management kubeconfig. StorageClasses and advertised DPF API groups are additional optional reads. Inventory mode creates no Pods and performs no management-network connectivity tests. It does not install DPF or run commands inside Kubernetes nodes.

transitions.label: Return facts and read failures to CLI

steps.title: CLI machine: match cards and assess results
steps.body:
Launch Kit compares physical card serials returned by the selected sources. Each explicit DPU must match exactly one adapter on one observed host. A missing serial, conflicting identity or multiple matches prevents a complete inventory; an IP address or PCI address cannot substitute for that match. With host-only input, the inventory lists host-reported BlueFields without claiming a working ARM or BMC connection. These records remain partial and fail the required DPU BMC administrator check; ARM SSH cannot bypass that requirement.

Next, the CLI compares eligible measured versions with the selected release's documented requirements. It reports unavailable measurements and unknown requirements separately from below-minimum versions. These comparisons do not install or update software.

If address lookup is configured, the CLI separately matches your supplied management MACs to local lease-file records and neighbors read from the selected SSH endpoints. These are unverified IP candidates, not card identities or host-to-DPU associations. No candidate is contacted automatically.

Finally, the CLI checks collection and session-cleanup results, compares against any previous inventory, and writes the YAML and report. Required failures produce partial output; optional gaps remain recorded even when inventory completes. All output files are written on the CLI machine.

steps.title: CLI machine: review inventory and reasons
steps.body:
The normal text summary shows the required-check result and named host/DPU mappings. It separates discovery blockers from later provisioning prerequisites and checks not requested. Repeated qualification/BOM gaps are grouped by affected sources; they do not mean a hardware failure was detected. Internal identity/comparison SHA identifiers remain in JSON/YAML, not as operator-facing device names. Both host and DPU results use named facts and field-specific issues; device evidence references, raw command strings and vendor firmware metadata are omitted. Saved YAML omits evidence maps and references from every source, including management, SSH, address lookup and connectivity probes. Diagnostic JSON is separate and can retain internal bookkeeping.

Inspect `discovery.outcome`, `discovery.checks`, `errors`, `artifacts` and `acceptance` in the JSON report. Review saved `inventory.hosts`, `inventory.dpus`, `inventory.associations` and field-specific issues before using the handoff. Complete discovery writes `dpf-discovered.yaml`; partial discovery preserves an existing handoff and writes `partial.yaml` and `report.json` under `dpf-discovered.discovery/<run-id>/`. Use the report's artifact paths instead of guessing the run ID.

Read each host/DPU `issues` entry's `field`, `code`, `message` and `tool` where present. Successful values live in named fields such as `psid`, `bmcAdministratorVerified`, `runtime.mftVersion` and `runtime.hardware.cards[].firmwareVersion`. Cards also retain typed `nextBoot` settings and `hostPrivileges`; next-boot values do not prove the running mode. A public `id` requires successful final identity rechecks; a serial retained on a failed record is diagnostic context. Generic observation maps and repeated successful state are omitted.

DPU `firmware` groups version lists by component, retaining known activation separately. `firmwareInventoryComplete: true` means enumeration completed, not that every version is known or compatible. ERoT firmware remains separate from BMC firmware. The JSON report retains all required check outcomes and deferred provisioning checks. New inventories use `v1alpha3`; the updated CLI also reads legacy `v1alpha1`/`v1alpha2` without inferring missing verification.

A missing `mlxfwmanager` is an unavailable prerequisite, not proof of incompatible NIC firmware. A denied Redfish firmware read differs from a property that is not exposed. Conflicting versions or unknown activation cannot establish a software minimum.

| Example reason | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE` / `PERMISSION_DENIED` | Check the named endpoint tool or authorized noninteractive sudo policy; do not treat the unmeasured check as passed. |
| `ACCESS_DENIED` / `PROPERTY_NOT_EXPOSED` | Distinguish an account permission problem from a property the service does not advertise. |
| `SOFTWARE_VERSION_CONFLICT` / `SOFTWARE_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE` | Reconcile version/activation sources or the rejected physical identity before trusting software comparisons. |
| `SOFTWARE_BELOW_MINIMUM` | Review the release requirement and plan a separate maintenance action; discovery does not update firmware. |
| `HOST_ADAPTER_VENDOR_CONFLICT` | Inspect the selected endpoints and matching serial/PCI evidence: a same-serial host adapter reports a non-NVIDIA vendor. Correct the source and rediscover; do not edit observed identity or discard a contradictory candidate to force a match. |
| `BMC_ADMIN_REQUIRED` / `BMC_ADMIN_ACCESS_DENIED` | Use an authorized account with all standard Administrator privileges and readable account/role evidence. |
| `BMC_ADMIN_UNVERIFIABLE` / `BMC_ADMIN_NOT_VERIFIED` | Supply explicit trusted DPU BMC access and inspect session Roles, authentication origin and linked account/role evidence. Host/ARM SSH and a same-named local administrator cannot substitute for verified session privileges. |
| `BMC_PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED` / `BMC_ADMIN_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTED` | Ask the administrator to resolve password-change, disabled or locked state separately, then rerun. Discovery does not repair access. |
| `PUBLICATION_FAILED` | Read the error explanation, resolve the local output/path problem, and rerun; only listed successfully written artifacts exist. |

The resolved software BOM is saved under `inventory.software`: operator/component coordinates, exact hardware models and BFB version/URL/known digest, with documented minima in named fields such as `minimumNICFirmware` and `minimumHostMFT`. Missing minima remain unknown; catalog sources/revisions and generic requirement lists are omitted. A missing artifact digest is not fabricated. Release `26.4.0` has exact BlueField-3 model entries `B3210`, `B3220` and `B3240`; generic family names and BlueField-4 are not sufficient for BOM applicability. The documented NIC/MFT minima can be evaluated when current measurements associated with the correct device exist. BMC, CEC, ATF, UEFI, OS/BSP and golden-image minima remain unknown where the catalog has no supported requirement. A BFB target is a desired artifact, not an observed OS/BSP version. An unknown requirement must remain unresolved; supplying a guessed minimum does not establish compatibility.

Exit zero and `discovery.outcome: complete` mean inventory collection, identity/mapping, cleanup and publication succeeded. `acceptance: not-evaluated` remains explicit. Hardware support, DPF authentication, service connectivity and deployment still need separate assessment; DPF generate/deploy/validate are unavailable in this preview.

steps.title: Endpoint owner or CLI operator: correct the cause
steps.body: Use the specific recorded reason to correct the source configuration or ask the infrastructure owner to repair missing tools, permissions, credentials, connectivity or conflicting identity. Do not delete unknown observations or label them passed. Optional gaps may remain documented without blocking inventory; required source failures, identity ambiguity, cleanup or publication errors need resolution. If cleanup is uncertain, use the reported session/resource ownership evidence before any manual action. Rerun after correcting the cause.

steps.title: CLI machine: retain the inventory and report
steps.body: Retain the seed, discovered YAML, JSON report and stderr log together. The discovered YAML preserves configuration intent and replaces observed inventory; it is not a deployment-ready profile or a provisioning approval. If a DPU access address is missing, use [address-candidate lookup](#address-candidates). For later remeasurement of the same estate, use [refresh](#refresh-inventory).

workflows.title: Find and verify address candidates
workflows.introduction: Use this optional inventory addition when you know an ARM or BMC management MAC but need its possible IP address. It is a locator workflow, not authentication or identity discovery. You still need the host configuration from the first workflow; this is not a standalone subnet scanner.

steps.title: CLI machine: prepare MACs and lease snapshots
steps.body:
Obtain the exact ARM or BMC management MAC from authoritative asset records or a trustworthy observed interface. You must choose its role (`arm` or `bmc`) and a unique name. Launch Kit does not infer a management MAC from a NIC serial, data-port MAC, hostname or neighboring address.

Optionally obtain a current dnsmasq IPv4 lease-file snapshot through your authorized DHCP administration process and place it on the CLI machine. Launch Kit reads this file locally; it does not log in to a DHCP server or query arbitrary vendor lease APIs. With no lease files, it can use suitable neighbors observed on the SSH endpoints already selected for inventory. Only `REACHABLE` or `PERMANENT` neighbors are candidates; stale entries are excluded.

steps.title: CLI machine: configure address lookup
steps.body:
Merge this fragment into the existing `discovery` section of a seed without saved inventory. Replace the MACs and file path; omit `sources` if you only want eligible observed neighbors. Do not replace the required host list.

```yaml
discovery:
  addressLookup:
    sources:
      - file: ./inputs/dnsmasq.leases
        format: dnsmasq-leases
    devices:
      - name: dpu-a-arm
        role: arm
        mac: '02:00:00:00:00:11'
      - name: dpu-a-bmc
        role: bmc
        mac: '02:00:00:00:00:12'
```

The supported file contains the five dnsmasq IPv4 columns: expiry epoch, MAC, IP, hostname and client ID. An expiry of `0` means a nonexpiring record; expired records are not candidates. Each file must be readable, at most 1 MiB and at most 4096 records. A malformed file contributes no candidates and retains a source failure reason. Other DHCP formats are unsupported.

steps.title: CLI machine: run inventory and local lookup
steps.body:
Save the configured seed as `dpf-lookup.yaml` and select a new handoff path.

```bash
l8k discover --target dpf --user-config dpf-lookup.yaml \
  --save-cluster-config dpf-candidates.yaml --output json \
  > candidates.json 2> candidates.log
```

The selected endpoints undergo the same [identity and optional reads](#initial-inventory-collect) as first inventory. On the CLI machine, address lookup then reads the configured lease snapshots and matches the supplied MACs against those records and the neighbors returned by remote `ip -j neighbor show`. No candidate is contacted and no credential is sent to it.

Watch live source/check status on stderr: RUNNING is emitted before the operation, followed by its result. Endpoint names/addresses distinguish concurrent work. To keep progress visible with JSON, redirect stdout only (`>discover.json`). Add `--log-level debug` for stage timing or `--log-level trace` for request/tool metadata; `2>discover.log` saves these messages instead of displaying them. Quiet suppresses progress.

steps.title: CLI operator: review candidate addresses
steps.body:
Read `inventory.addressLookup.candidates` for the address, selected name/role/MAC and source. Read `inventory.addressLookup.observations` for each device and lease source. A single address is `ADDRESS_UNVERIFIED`; several addresses for a MAC remain ambiguous, and missing/expired/unreadable evidence keeps its reason. A candidate is not a host-to-DPU association and is never a readiness pass.

Use your DHCP/network or asset owner to resolve multiple, missing or contradictory locators. Do not choose an address merely because it is the first result. Independent identity and endpoint trust are still required even for one candidate.

steps.title: Endpoint owner and CLI operator: verify and select
steps.body:
Verify endpoint ownership and obtain SSH known-hosts trust or Redfish CA trust and the appropriate account through your normal process. Create a new seed and add the verified endpoint under `discovery.dpus`, with its credential reference and trust policy. Use a new output when changing scope; do not edit the old observed identity to force a match.

Run [initial inventory](#initial-inventory) for that explicit endpoint. Only its authenticated physical-card observation and unique host-card association can establish the binding. A discovered IP alone never authorizes Redfish access or proves Zero Trust attestation.

workflows.title: Refresh an existing inventory
workflows.introduction: Use this workflow to remeasure the same selected estate, compare facts and preserve diagnostic history. A refresh is another live read; old successful observations do not stand in for unavailable current measurements.

steps.title: CLI machine: check inputs and trust before refresh
steps.body:
Start from the existing discovered YAML and keep its credential/trust references valid. Decide whether you are remeasuring the same host/DPU endpoints and trust policy. If endpoint selection, trust policy or physical identity has changed, create a fresh input without old `inventory` and use a new output path. Investigate unexpected replacement or ownership changes before accepting them.

The saved `scopeDigest` guards resolved endpoint/trust selection; the inventory does not repeat the configured policy list as `requestedScope`. Removing private device provenance alone is not a physical change.

Changing Redfish certificate verification or the contents of a custom CA file requires a new inventory. Moving an unchanged CA file to another path does not. Keep the CLI machine's operating-system trust store maintained; discovery does not report changes within that store.

The CLI reads legacy `v1alpha1` and `v1alpha2` inventories conservatively, but some older identity/trust bindings cannot support safe refresh. If the command reports that the old inventory is incompatible, verify endpoint ownership, create a fresh input without saved `inventory`, and use a new output path. Keep the previous file as history; do not edit its recorded identities or trust information to bypass the error.

Do not manually edit observed serials, associations, firmware or check outcomes. `dpf.release` selects the release's BOM; changing it does not upgrade software. An omitted release uses the CLI's default, so record the CLI version and review `inventory.software` when comparing runs from different versions. Specify the release explicitly when you want to retain that choice.

steps.title: CLI machine: repeat reads on the selected endpoints
steps.body:
Launch Kit repeats the [same reads on the selected host, DPU, BMC and optional management API](#initial-inventory-collect), then matches the returned identities and compares them with the saved inventory. Run from the CLI machine using the same YAML path for input and output and explicitly supply `--save-cluster-config`:

```bash
l8k discover --target dpf --user-config dpf-discovered.yaml \
  --save-cluster-config dpf-discovered.yaml --output json \
  > refresh.json 2> refresh.log
```

A complete in-place refresh retains `source-before.yaml` before replacing inventory while preserving user sections, comments and input intent. A partial run leaves the original input unchanged and writes its new observations separately; it does not create this backup. Relative file references are rebased if saving elsewhere; private files are not copied. Avoid simultaneous external edits, and use real output directories rather than symlink aliases. Credentials, trust files and configured lease files cannot be used as output destinations.

Watch live source/check status on stderr: RUNNING is emitted before the operation, followed by its result. Endpoint names/addresses distinguish concurrent work. To keep progress visible with JSON, redirect stdout only (`>discover.json`). Add `--log-level debug` for stage timing or `--log-level trace` for request/tool metadata; `2>discover.log` saves these messages instead of displaying them. Quiet suppresses progress.

steps.title: CLI machine: compare new observations and reasons
steps.body:
Review `diff`, current checks, `errors`, cleanup and successfully written `artifacts` in the result. Compare physical identity, firmware, relevant hardware/mode/network observations and resolved release requirements. A failed current observation stays unknown rather than inheriting an earlier pass. Reordered lists alone are not changes to the observed configuration.

On partial collection, the previous handoff remains intact and the new partial YAML/report live under `dpf-discovered.discovery/<run-id>/`. Inspect the new report instead of mistaking the unchanged handoff for fresh success. Required failures need correction and another run. Optional missing tools or inaccessible properties remain explained observations; they do not make deployment readiness pass.

steps.title: Endpoint owner or CLI operator: repair and retry
steps.body: Use the saved reason and affected source to repair the external prerequisite or fix the input. Preserve the unsuccessful run's report. Do not overwrite failure evidence with an old successful observation. If the cause is a real endpoint, trust or identity change, switch to a fresh seed and output.

steps.title: CLI machine: start a new inventory
steps.body: Create a new seed from the desired access configuration, without copying old `inventory` facts, and select a new handoff path. Recheck endpoint ownership/trust and follow [initial inventory](#initial-inventory). Keep the previous estate's handoff and report as history.

steps.title: CLI machine: retain the refreshed files
steps.body: Keep the current YAML, JSON/stdout report and stderr log, plus `source-before.yaml` when a complete in-place refresh created it. Discovery completion still means a successful inventory workflow, with deployment `acceptance: not-evaluated`. Unknown software requirements and unverified deployment prerequisites remain unresolved; a refreshed inventory does not enable DPF deployment.

workflows.title: Test management-network paths
workflows.introduction: Use explicit management mode to check connections from the management cluster and inspect the node interfaces needed for a new DPF tenant. See [probe prerequisites](dpf-discovery.md#management-network-probes). Inventory-only discovery remains available without these temporary resources.

steps.title: CLI operator: enable management mode and select access
steps.body: Set `discovery.probes.mode: management`, an explicit management kubeconfig, and an existing probe namespace. Retain the selected DPU BMC endpoints. Provide public CA files where needed. An explicit BMC TLS bypass also applies to that BMC’s probe; its successful handshake is reported as unverified. Management API TLS verification remains required. For HBN-BGP, supply `provisioning.bootstrap.tenant.vip`, `interface`, and any node-selector override. The account needs namespace/Node reads and temporary Pod/ConfigMap create, inspect, log-read and delete permissions. Nodes must be Ready, schedulable Linux/amd64; admission must allow the requested non-root host-network Pods. Launch Kit does not change cluster policy.

steps.title: Management cluster: run bounded network probes
steps.body: The CLI validates the complete management-node scope before creating a request ConfigMap. On each node it schedules one ordinary Pod-network probe and one host-network probe using the pinned published diagnostic image. Each checks address resolution, TCP and HTTPS to the management API and selected DPU BMCs. API certificates are always verified. BMC probes follow each endpoint’s explicit trust policy; a bypassed certificate remains reported as unverified even when the connection succeeds. The host-network probe also reads interface addresses/link state and routes, and performs a kernel route lookup for a configured HBN tenant VIP. No credentials are copied into Pods and no node or switch settings are changed. Live progress identifies the node and network namespace. A failed network path does not suppress independent probes, but remains a failed result. Admission, image, identity, invalid-response or deadline failures stop collection.

steps.title: CLI machine: remove owned probe resources
steps.body: The CLI removes only the temporary Pods and ConfigMap it created, checking their recorded UIDs and ownership. It records leftovers if cleanup cannot complete. Keep the report and resource journal when diagnosing a failure; do not remove another run’s resources.

steps.title: CLI operator: distinguish path checks from allocation
steps.body: Review every failed or unknown path and each selected node’s interface/tenant-VIP route check. Missing facts, a down interface, an off-link route or a VIP already assigned to a selected node block new-tenant readiness. Passing these checks establishes current node network facts only. Supply the three tenant.allocation declarations only after confirming VIP reservation, DHCP exclusion and VRRP ID availability on the selected control-plane nodes with the site owner. Missing declarations remain unknown and false declarations fail readiness. True values are site declarations, not independently measured IPAM facts; they cannot override an observed collision. DNS/ARP silence or absence from a DPUCluster list cannot prove an allocation. For another tenant with the same VRRP ID, Launch Kit compares control-plane node selectors: potentially overlapping placement fails, disjoint selectors do not conflict, and missing selector facts remain unknown. A cluster with no Keepalived endpoint does not reserve a VIP or VRRP ID through that configuration.

steps.title: Infrastructure owner: resolve the reported prerequisite
steps.body: Use the saved reason to correct trust, access, node state, desired interface/VIP, routing or incomplete cleanup. Arrange infrastructure changes with the responsible owner. Discovery does not apply switch configuration or reserve addresses. Rerun after the cause is resolved.

steps.title: CLI operator: retain the observations
steps.body: Keep the saved inventory, report and logs. The HBN readiness report still requires all other deployment prerequisites; successful network probes do not mean DPF or HBN has been deployed.

workflows.title: Check HBN-BGP fabric prerequisites
workflows.introduction: Run this additional preflight for the independent HBN-BGP use case. Physical inventory and use-case readiness are separate results. See [HBN-BGP inputs](dpf-discovery.md#check-hbn-bgp-prerequisites) for the site fields and defaults.

steps.title: CLI operator: select the desired profile and switch access
steps.body:
Retain explicit host and DPU BMC targets. Add each switch SSH address, credential reference, pinned known-hosts file and intended p0/p1-to-switch-port bindings. Omit networking fields to use defaults or override them in `dpf.hbn`. Supply the tenant VIP and control-plane management interface under `provisioning.bootstrap.tenant`; discovery can reuse a literal observed management API IP and port. Missing allocations remain blockers. HBN software and node-effect defaults can be overridden under `provisioning.hbn`. Unknown cabling must remain unresolved; do not guess a mapping from LLDP names.

The selected HBN-BGP profile supplies the expected network configuration. Omit `dpf.hbn` to use its defaults, or override individual VRF, ASN, MTU and address-pool fields for your environment. Discovery compares the live fabric with these resolved values; it does not adopt conflicting switch settings as new defaults. Generation uses the same effective configuration. Keep credentials, access endpoints and physical port bindings in their separate site inputs.

steps.title: CLI machine: run HBN-BGP discovery
steps.body:
Run `l8k discover --target dpf --use-case hbn-bgp --user-config dpf-site.yaml --save-cluster-config dpf-discovered.yaml`. The CLI reads host/DPU identity and authorization, management observations when configured, and read-only switch facts. The switch SSH session reads the NVUE revision table before and after collecting facts. The explicit active application must remain stable and match exactly one saved-history record. Missing, ambiguous, changing or unsupported state and unconfirmed changes block readiness, even when an older applied alias still matches a saved record. Historical saved revisions and unrelated staged changes can remain present. This check does not inspect startup-file contents or test persistence through a reboot.

Host SSH checks selected PCI functions, drivers, IOMMU groups and management-path separation. It reads each PCI-associated interface's permanent hardware MAC with ethtool -P, checking the sysfs PCI binding before and after the read. The saved permanentMAC is separate from the current mac; missing tools or inconsistent bindings retain an unavailable reason.

The same host SSH access inspects the selected p0's active networkd mapping and merged Netplan configuration. This backend requires Ubuntu 24.04, Netplan 1.1.2, systemd-networkd 255, iproute2 6.1.0 and installed host tools including jq, dmidecode, lspci and ethtool. It checks root access, permanent-MAC/name binding, supported interface settings and kernel MTU limits. Missing tools or limits, conflicting identity, unsupported manager/DHCP/policy/default routes and an unsupported desired workload MTU block the result with a reason. The desired MTU comes from the same resolved profile used by generation; a different current MTU is a planned change when supported. The current backend requires both current and desired workload MTUs of at least 1280; crossing that boundary can remove or create existing IPv6 state. Kernel capability and backend support are checked separately. An unsupported explicit override remains unchanged and blocks readiness. Raw merged configuration is not saved or logged. This is read-only inspection: it does not generate files, reload managers or configure links. Exact host address and route checks wait for the actual DPF allocation. A backend pass is not an applied address, persistence or traffic result. The flat host route supports one selected DPU per physical host.

DPU Redfish verifies the selected release’s initial enrollment reads as well as physical identity. An older BMC may support inventory while lacking the fixed chassis, PSID or PF0 resources required by DPF; the missing resource blocks readiness with a compatibility explanation. These reads do not exercise controller authentication or provisioning writes. DPU Redfish reads card-owned network-function MACs; unique switch LLDP MAC and p0/p1 claims corroborate uplink bindings. For unresolved bindings, host SSH can receive LLDP with existing tcpdump and timeout tools for up to 65 seconds per selected physical interface. Current UUID, card serial, PCI and physical-port identities are rechecked; switch chassis, system name and port must match authenticated switch observations. Expired or conflicting advertisements cannot pass, and the fallback never overrides a known mismatch. Raw packets are not saved in the discovered configuration.

Management API reads check Kamaji default datastore validation, its linked etcd replicas and pods, bound claims and volumes, and the local-path provisioner. Missing, denied, stale or mismatched storage observations block readiness; these reads do not measure remaining disk capacity. When provisioning inputs and current identities are complete, the CLI downloads and verifies the selected charts, derives the management deployment plan, and asks the management API to check the configured caller’s scoped permissions. Missing plan inputs, failed chart validation and denied or incomplete authorization responses block readiness. These authorization reviews do not install the generated resources.

NVUE reads applied and operational configuration, including per-port queries for the selected uplinks; FRR supplies current BGP state and running configuration. The policy check resolves selected peers and inherited groups; a verified unfiltered flat baseline can pass, but unsupported filters remain explained unknowns. It does not verify future advertised or accepted routes. The CLI checks list/detail consistency and does not infer routed membership from an absent bridge field. It also reads the switch’s local LLDP chassis identity through authenticated SSH; the configured display name is not physical identity. Only protected LLDP/FRR reads use configured sudo. No switch configuration is changed. Set `discovery.probes.mode: management` to add the [management-network workflow](#management-network), including selected-interface and tenant-VIP route checks. This mode creates temporary Pods and a request ConfigMap; inventory mode does not.

steps.title: CLI operator: review inventory and readiness separately
steps.body: Inspect `discovery.outcome`, `readiness.state`, each failed readiness check, and the command exit status. Complete physical inventory may be saved even when HBN-BGP readiness is blocked. Missing required facts, mismatched VRF/ASN/MTU, absent unnumbered neighbors and unknown uplink mapping cannot count as passes. Discovery retains unverified provisioning prerequisites as deploy-phase blockers. BGP establishment and traffic validation are post-deployment checks.

steps.title: Infrastructure owner: resolve the reported cause
steps.body:
Correct access or desired inputs, or arrange the needed infrastructure change with its owner. Defaults are desired values, not permission to reconfigure a switch. Review switch changes separately. Preserve the recorded reason and rerun after correction; do not edit observations to force a pass.

A manual switch inspection can help diagnose a failed check, but it does not turn that check into a pass. Rerun discovery after correcting the configuration or supplying the missing supported observation. Discovery does not apply switch changes; those require a separate configuration operation.

steps.title: CLI operator: retain the handoff and verification limits
steps.body: Keep the saved configuration and report. Passing prerequisite checks does not establish live BGP adjacency, workload traffic or production hardware qualification. Those require the deployment and validation workflow.

workflows.title: Generate HBN-BGP deployment files
workflows.introduction: Run generation on the CLI machine after collecting the selected estate. A blocked readiness result can still be used to prepare manifests, provided required generation inputs are complete. Deployment must resolve and recheck the blockers. See [generation inputs and outputs](dpf-generation.md).

steps.title: CLI operator: complete the saved site configuration
steps.body: Keep the discovered inventory in the site file. Supply the reserved tenant API VIP/interface and explicit tenant.allocation declarations, the hardware-specific DPUFlavor spec, and the HTTPS OS ISO and PSID-specific PLDM URLs with SHA-256 digests. Review profile defaults and override only the values needed for your site. Endpoint credentials remain references; generation does not read them. The default BMC reset policy is Never. An OnInitialization override requires verified DHCP recovery to the same BMC addresses before enrollment; a reset clears existing BMC networking.

steps.title: CLI machine: resolve and check selected identities
steps.body: Run `l8k generate --target dpf --use-case hbn-bgp --user-config dpf-site.yaml --save-deployment-files ./hbn-bgp`. Launch Kit matches the selected source endpoints to the saved DPU identities and host associations, verifies that administrator access was recorded, and resolves exact PSIDs and desired settings. Missing identities or required inputs stop generation before chart downloads. Host address index 2 and gateway index 1 default from the profile and may be overridden under provisioning.hbn. They must be different usable addresses in every per-DPU subnet; plans requiring more than 4096 subnet reservations are rejected.

steps.title: CLI machine: retrieve charts and validate resources
steps.body: The CLI downloads the selected DPF operator and HBN chart archives over HTTPS and verifies their recorded SHA-256 digests and metadata. It renders management bootstrap and HBN manifests locally, checks custom-resource structure against the selected operator schemas, and validates the complete artifact bundle. It does not connect to or modify the management cluster, hosts, DPUs or switches. A render or validation failure leaves the destination untouched. The interface manifests carry selectors derived from the selected DPU cluster and DPU node names. Generation does not check whether live labels uniquely identify those targets. HBN resource requests are included in both the container configuration and DPF service capacity accounting. The workload IPAM manifest excludes the selected host address from ordinary dynamic allocation in every possible DPU subnet. It does not assign subnets to specific DPUs or configure host addresses and routes.

steps.title: CLI machine: save a complete bundle
steps.body: A new directory is published only after all files validate. A byte-identical existing bundle is unchanged; a different or incomplete destination is rejected. Choose a new directory when changing the desired deployment. Retain the original site YAML, resolved configuration, verified archives and ordered manifests together.

steps.title: CLI operator: correct the reported problem
steps.body: Correct the named input or archive problem. Rerun discovery if device selection or identity has changed; do not edit observations to manufacture a successful check. Choose a new destination if the previous directory contains a different bundle. Rerun generation after correcting the cause.

steps.title: CLI operator: review artifacts and remaining readiness checks
steps.body: Review the tenant endpoint, selected DPU serials, software URLs, flavor settings and HBN network allocation. Generation success proves that local artifacts were constructed and validated; it does not prove API admission, artifact consumption, tenant health, live BGP sessions or workload traffic. A separate `l8k deploy --target dpf` command can execute the reviewed bundle after fresh deployment checks pass; follow the [HBN-BGP deployment procedure](#hbn-bgp-deployment).

workflows.title: Deploy and validate HBN-BGP
workflows.introduction: Use this procedure after a complete HBN-BGP discovery and a reviewed generated bundle. Deployment is a separate live operation: it can create management and tenant resources, enroll and provision selected DPUs, request guarded host resets, configure selected host PF networking, and run post-join HBN/BGP/traffic checks. It does not configure switches or establish general hardware qualification. For the full stage order and decisions, see the [DPF deployment guide](dpf-deployment.md).

steps.title: CLI operator: confirm site inputs and defaults
steps.body:
Start from the site file used by discovery and retain the discovered inventory. Supply explicit DPU BMC Administrator access, host SSH identities/trust, management kubeconfig reference and selected switch read access. Set `dpf.useCase: hbn-bgp`; the profile provides release and HBN defaults unless overridden. Review the resolved VRF, fabric ASN, DPU ASN range, uplink/workload MTUs and IP pools against the intended fabric.

Before any DPU installation effect, establish the selected switch configuration and port bindings with the fabric owner. The deployment command observes switch state; it does not apply switch changes. Review the generated HBN `DPUServiceConfiguration` and `DPUDeployment` declarations before deploy so the selected VRF, BGP ASN/neighbors, MTUs and host-facing service chain are the intended values. The running HBN service cannot be ready until the selected DPU has installed its OS, joined through DPF and received the service resources.

Supply the site tenant VIP, control-plane interface and VRID under `provisioning.bootstrap.tenant`. Also supply all three explicit site declarations under `provisioning.bootstrap.tenant.allocation`: `vipReserved`, `vipExcludedFromDHCP` and `routerIDUniqueOnSelectedNodes`. Each must be true only when backed by the responsible allocation/VRRP authority. No profile default exists for these values; a quiet ARP probe or an absent current tenant does not prove DHCP exclusion or reservation. Keep the independent control-plane MTU separate from HBN uplink/workload MTUs. Provisioning artifacts, flavor and resources must match the selected hardware/release cohort; a syntactically valid URL and digest do not establish vendor qualification.

For accepted inputs, DPU BMC reset policy defaults to `Never`. Selecting `OnInitialization` requires a known recovery path to the same BMC addresses. Do not include host PF addresses observed during a previous run: deployment must use the actual per-DPU IPAM allocation.

steps.title: CLI machine: collect a fresh deployment inventory
steps.body:
Run discovery from the machine that has network access to the selected endpoints:

```bash
l8k discover --target dpf --use-case hbn-bgp \
  --user-config dpf-site.yaml \
  --save-cluster-config dpf-discovered.yaml \
  --output json
```

The CLI reads local site/trust files and writes the handoff locally. It connects to configured hosts over pinned SSH, selected DPU BMCs over HTTPS Redfish, the management Kubernetes API through the configured kubeconfig, and selected switches over pinned SSH for read-only NVUE/kernel observations. It does not SSH into DPU ARM for provisioning and does not change switch configuration. If management network probes are configured, discovery may use temporary probe resources as documented in the discovery guide.

Inspect `discovery.outcome`, `readiness.state`, each check's state/reason, command exit status and stderr. A complete inventory is not deploy readiness: required unknown or failed checks block. Optional unknown observations stay unknown; they are not passes. Resolve the recorded cause with the responsible owner and perform a new discovery. Do not edit observations to force readiness.

transitions.label: Required check unknown, failed or stale

steps.title: CLI operator: verify deployment gates
steps.body:
Continue only when the fresh report is complete and `readiness.state` is `ready` for HBN-BGP deployment. Confirm the management cluster identity and access, selected host/DPU serial and PSID bindings, BMC Administrator proof, host/PCI and management-path separation, supported host network backend, switch port/VRF/ASN/BGP policy facts, exact software cohort and all tenant allocation declarations. Confirm the tenant VIP/interface/VRID and selected control-plane nodes still match the authorized site plan.

Readiness checks are point-in-time facts. A prior discovery, successful manual run or current Kubernetes object does not replace them. If an ASIC property or another hardware state has no supported measurement, it remains unmeasured; NVUE/kernel configuration alone does not prove ASIC programming. Complete any separately authorized vendor recovery or hardware preparation before deploy, and do not turn a one-off recovery action into an automatic retry.

steps.title: CLI machine: build the reviewed local bundle
steps.body:
Generate from the fresh discovered handoff:

```bash
l8k generate --target dpf --use-case hbn-bgp \
  --user-config dpf-discovered.yaml \
  --save-deployment-files ./hbn-bgp \
  --output json
```

Generation runs locally. It resolves selected identities and profile defaults/overrides, retrieves the pinned DPF operator and HBN chart archives, checks their digests, renders the management and workload resources and validates them against the selected schemas. It does not contact Kubernetes, hosts, DPUs, BMCs or switches and makes no remote changes. Generation failure means there is no new accepted bundle; retain the error reason and correct the input/source before retrying.

steps.title: CLI operator: inspect desired effects before deployment
steps.body:
Review `./hbn-bgp` and its retained metadata before allowing effects. Check the exact DPU serial/PSID selectors, operator release, provisioning flavor, software URLs/digests, tenant endpoint and site allocation declarations. Inspect `DPFOperatorConfig.spec.networking.highSpeedMTU` separately from `controlPlaneMTU`. Inspect the HBN startup settings and all three service-chain `serviceMTU` values: p0/p1 follow `uplinkMTU`; pf0hpf and the host PF follow `workloadMTU`. Confirm the profile's actual VRF/ASN and address-pool values and that the switch is already configured to match.

Do not deploy when tenant reservation, DHCP exclusion, VRID authority, artifact applicability, selected device identity, host backend, required management checks or fabric checks are unknown/failed. The deployment guide describes every stage and expected effect. The `dpf` target requires explicit `--user-config` and `--deployment-files`; it does not use Host `--kubeconfig`, `--dry-run` or `--overwrite-existing`. Deployment defaults to two hours and accepts no timeout above two hours.

Use the standalone `discover`, `generate` and `deploy` commands shown here. `l8k validate --target dpf`, the root `pipeline` command for DPF, and `l8k generate --target dpf --deploy` are not enabled.

steps.title: CLI machine and DPF controllers: execute the live workflow
steps.body:
Run the separate deployment command from a machine that can reach the management API, selected host SSH endpoints, selected BMCs and switches:

```bash
l8k deploy --target dpf \
  --user-config dpf-discovered.yaml \
  --deployment-files ./hbn-bgp \
  --deploy-timeout 2h \
  --output json
```

`--deploy-timeout` is optional; the default is two hours and the maximum is two hours. Both file arguments are required explicitly for DPF. The CLI reads the configured management kubeconfig and performs fresh checks before effects. Do not pass `--kubeconfig`, `--dry-run` or `--overwrite-existing`; those are not supported by DPF. There is no automatic cleanup of a conflicting deployment.

The CLI talks to the management Kubernetes API to install/wait for DPF and create/verify tenant resources. After the tenant API becomes available, the CLI rechecks DPF operator configuration readiness. If the operator reports startup is still in progress, the CLI waits within the deployment deadline before enrollment. Changed identities, ownership, desired configuration or release version stop the run. DPF controllers then use configured DPU BMC credentials for enrollment and OS/software installation. Launch Kit does not run installation commands over DPU ARM SSH. When DPF requests an external reset, Launch Kit only performs a supported system-level host reset over the selected host's pinned SSH after checking the exact request, device identity and shutdown state. A required DPU PowerCycle, unknown reset method or unmeasurable safety state stops with a reason; it is never guessed. Host SSH is also used for fresh network inspection and, after allocation, the selected host PF address/route configuration. Switch SSH remains read-only.

At boot, network readiness follows each selected host port's existing Netplan optionality. A required port's static workload address joins Netplan's "any routable interface" wait, so that wait can succeed through the workload port. Launch Kit checks management reachability separately.

After the DPU agent joins, DPF applies HBN and Launch Kit waits for the current selected service/interface resources and actual HBN containers. It reads each HBN's BGP peers and installed routes, then tests traffic for every directed selected-host pair, including ordinary and DF traffic at the configured workload MTU. Host network addresses are based on the actual DPF IPAM allocation, not index guesses or addresses retained from an earlier manual run.

steps.title: CLI operator: distinguish provisioning from validation
steps.body:
In text output, inspect the reported state, last completed stage and report path. With `--output json`, retain stdout as the structured result and stderr separately. The run creates an `l8k-dpf-deploy-*` report directory beside the bundle; preserve its deployment and probe records. A failed or interrupted run can leave earlier management, tenant, enrollment, firmware, host-network or HBN effects in place.

A one-host run may finish `provisioned`; that does not establish cross-host traffic. Treat a multi-host run as `validated` only when the selected BGP sessions, installed routes, all directed ordinary traffic and DF MTU checks passed. Neither state is general hardware qualification or proof of every failover mode. If a failure, unavailable check or timeout occurs, inspect the report and current live resources/device state before any further attempt. Correct source inputs and regenerate when desired state changed. Never blindly replay an ambiguous reset, delete pending annotations or edit observed resource status.

steps.title: CLI operator: preserve the reason and reconcile partial state
steps.body: Keep the failed report, stdout, stderr and saved discovery handoff. Use each check's state, reason code and evidence reference to identify which required fact, external authority or operation failed. Unknown is not a pass. Resolve the issue with its owner, re-observe current state, and do not replay a command whose effect may have occurred. Before retrying, account for resources and device/host state left by earlier successful stages. If the site file or selected identity changes, rediscover and generate a new reviewed bundle. Deployment does not automatically delete earlier resources or vendor recovery state.

transitions.label: Correct site inputs or owner prerequisites
Refresh observations after live state changes
